In this section, we use data from Environmental Data Initiative (EDI) on Coastal Giant Salamanders collected in HJ Andrews Experimental Forest, Oregon. Measurements were taken in two sections of Mack Creek: one located in old-growth forest (OG) and the other in a clear-cut area (CC) harvested in 1963. The dataset is extracted from the `and_vertebrates` dataset of the `R` package `lterdatasampler`.

Forest harvesting can influence stream conditions, which may affect salamander growth and body size. A scientist is interested in testing whether there is a difference in average weight of Coastal Giant Salamanders between OG and CC. We will use a two-sample test to assess whether salamander size differs significantly between the two sites. Denoting by $\mu_{OG}$ and $\mu_{CC}$ the expected weight of the salamanders from the old-growth forest and from the clear-cut area, the hypotheses are

$$H_0: \mu_{OG} = \mu_{CC} \quad \text{and} \quad H_a: \mu_{OG} \neq \mu_{CC}.$$

## Solution



**Function reference:** `read_csv` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_pandas.qmd#pandas-read-csv); `head` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_pandas.qmd#pandas-head); `plt.figure` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_visualisation.qmd#plotting-plt-figure); `ax.boxplot` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_visualisation.qmd#plotting-ax-boxplot); `dict` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_python.qmd#python-dict); `ax.set_ylabel` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_visualisation.qmd#plotting-ax-set-ylabel); `plt.show` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_visualisation.qmd#plotting-plt-show).

```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df_salamander = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ELSTE-Master/Data-Science/main/Data/salamander_weights.csv")
df_salamander.head()

# Variable of interest
weight_CC = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="CC"]
weight_OG = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="OG"]

# Side-by-side boxplot
plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
plt.boxplot([weight_CC, weight_OG],    #<1>
            labels=["CC", "OG"],
            patch_artist=True,  # color the boxes
            boxprops=dict(facecolor="lightblue", color="blue"),
            medianprops=dict(color="red"))

plt.ylabel("Weight (g)")
plt.show()
```

### Question 2
One of your colleagues ran the following test to compare the two locations (OG and CC):

**Function reference:** `read_csv` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_pandas.qmd#pandas-read-csv); `stats.ttest_ind` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_numpy_scipy.qmd#numerical-stats-ttest-ind); `print` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_python.qmd#python-print).

```{python}
#| echo: true
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
df_salamander = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ELSTE-Master/Data-Science/main/Data/salamander_weights.csv")

# Variable of interest
weight_CC = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="CC"]
weight_OG = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="OG"]
# Perform independent two-sample t-test (assuming unequal variances)
t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(weight_CC, weight_OG, equal_var=False)

print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.3f}")
print(f"p-value: {p_val:.3f}")
```

The colleague concludes that there is no evidence from the data to suggest that the average weight of Coastal Giant Salamanders differs between the two locations. What do you think of this procedure?

### Question 4
Complete the code below to test whether the average size of Coastal Giant Salamanders differs between the two locations (OG and CC) using the appropriate test you selected in Question 3.

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: ex_7
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats

df_salamander = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ELSTE-Master/Data-Science/main/Data/salamander_weights.csv")
df_salamander.head()

# Variable of interest
weight_CC = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="CC"]
weight_OG = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="OG"]

stat, p_value = ______(weight_CC, weight_OG)
print(f"Mann-Whitney U test statistic: {stat}")
print(f"p-value: {p_value}")

```

## Hints

Consider using the function `mannwhitneyu()` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_numpy_scipy.qmd#numerical-stats-mannwhitneyu) from `scipy.stats`.


## Solution



**Function reference:** `read_csv` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_pandas.qmd#pandas-read-csv); `head` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_pandas.qmd#pandas-head); `stats.mannwhitneyu` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_numpy_scipy.qmd#numerical-stats-mannwhitneyu); `print` [(doc)](../appendices/doc_python.qmd#python-print).

```python
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats

df_salamander = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ELSTE-Master/Data-Science/main/Data/salamander_weights.csv")
df_salamander.head()

# Variable of interest
weight_CC = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="CC"]
weight_OG = df_salamander["weight_g"][df_salamander["section"]=="OG"]

stat, p_value = stats.mannwhitneyu(weight_CC, weight_OG)
print(f"Mann-Whitney U test statistic: {stat}")
print(f"P-value: {p_value}")
```
